about: The models the real duck runs now, by controller mode: try these first. pi/launcher.py reads its models from here (a --model in --stand-args / --emote-args is replaced by this one), so this file is what the duck actually runs. Change a model here, then bash pi/deploy.sh and restart the launcher (systemctl --user restart duck-launcher).

stand.what: the stable stand: X nods with mmh, Y says yes, B says no, the right stick and d-pad move the head
stand.status: stands the real duck steadily, recovers from nudges (flat feet, no soft soles)

emote.what: standing, plays microduck's 13 emotions: RB / LB the next / previous one, X again
emote.status: stable on the real duck, takes recovery steps; head moves at 70 %, smoothed. Keep a hand near for sad and devastated

head.what: sitting: the 13 emotions on the head and beak, no policy (head_pad.py, poses/sit_emote.json)
head.status: all 13 work on the real duck

walk_bam.what: the BAM walk: stands up, the left stick walks it (RT held: faster), the right stick turns it; RT + A sits it down
walk_bam.status: tried on the real duck 2026-11-25: stays up and steps steadily, but keeps stepping at a zero command and barely travels (in simulation 0.08 m/s for a 0.2 m/s command; turning works). Not a walk yet: keep a hand near

walk.what: LT + A: no walk is active there; the BAM walk is on RT + Y (walk_bam above)
walk.status: the walk models on LT + A were trained on a plain motor model, not BAM
